============================================================
Member support baseline — BEFORE apply

WHAT EXISTS
  is_ops_admin()        absent
  support_actions       absent
  support_lookup / support_can / support_log / support_recent   all absent

THE PREDICTION (written before applying)
  One new table appears, EMPTY: support_actions, the audit trail. Five new
  functions appear. Nothing existing is read, written or deleted.

  support_actions gets exactly ONE policy, and it is read-only, for ops admins.
  There is deliberately no insert, update or delete policy: rows are written
  only by support_log(), and NOBODY can amend or delete one -- including the
  person whose action it records. The migration refuses to finish if the policy
  count is not exactly 1.

  is_ops_admin() is defined as "every admin is an ops admin" for now. That
  means France gains the ability to trigger a member password reset today, and
  LOSES IT when M3 lands and replaces the body of that one function. That is
  intended and is the reason the gate exists as its own function rather than
  calling is_admin() directly at each site.

  IF IT IS WRONG: the audit table could be readable by someone who should not
  read it, or the rate limits could fail open. No member data is modified and
  no email is sent by this file -- sending is the Edge Function's job, and it
  is deployed separately. Undo with migrations/rollback-support-audit.sql.
